= Tenant
:page-aliases: operation::configuration/cache/tenant.adoc
:description: Wraps another cache to add in separation by tenant.
:page-eyebrow: Cache
:page-config-name: tenant
:page-related: cache/index.adoc[Cache Overview], authentication/index.adoc[Authentication Overview], operation::howto/multi-tenant.adoc, operation::examples/multi-tenant.adoc

== Description

This cache should be used in a multi-tenant deployment whenever a custom provider varies its output per tenant (e.g. different imagery or authorization per organization).

The tenant ID is populated by xref:authentication/index.adoc[authentication]. A request with no tenant ID falls back to the same cache key it would use without this wrapper, making this utterly pointless for a single-tenant (or unauthenticated) deployment.

The xref:commands::seed.adoc[seed] and xref:commands::test.adoc[test] commands have no incoming request to take a tenant from, so pass one with their `--tenant` flag. Without it they act on the un-namespaced key rather than any tenant's.

NOTE: Tenant IDs are subject to the same sanitization as layer names. That is, non-alphanumeric characters will be replaced with an underscore in some cases. If your tenant IDs differ by only special characters, rethink your tenant IDs.

== Example
[tabs]
====
YAML::
+
[,yaml]
----
cache:
  name: tenant
  cache:
    name: disk
    path: "./disk_tile_cache"
----

JSON::
+
[,json]
----
{
  "cache": {
    "name": "tenant",
    "cache": {
      "name": "disk",
      "path": "./disk_tile_cache"
    }
  }
}
----
====

== Configuration

.Configuration options
[cols="1m,3,1,1,1"]
|===
| Parameter | Description | Type | Required | Default

| Cache
